Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

across preposition and adverb

to or on the other side of

also over (a river, a wall), on the other side of, cross

classical

Catull. 11.9: sīve trāns altās gradiētur Alpēs
Cic. Att. 12.19.1: trāns Tiberim hortōs aliquōs parāre

trāns (+ accusative)

preposition with the accusative

across, over, on the far side of

Going across, or lying on the far side: trāns Tiberim, across the Tiber. For “opposite”, across the street from, see opposite.

Other words

  • trānseō, trānsīre, trānsiī, trānsitum — go across, cross

    verb, irregular (like eō), with the accusative · classical · Plin. NH 8.11: amnem trānsitūrī

    Latin often puts “across” in the verb and the thing crossed in the accusative: flūmen trānsīre, cross the river; trādūcere, take across; trānāre, swim across.

Examples

  • sīve trāns altās gradiētur Alpēs

    or whether he marches across the high AlpsCatull. 11.9

  • cōgitō interdum trāns Tiberim hortōs aliquōs parāre

    I sometimes think of getting a garden across the TiberCic. Att. 12.19.1

  • spēs ūnica imperiī populī Rōmānī L. Quīnctius trāns Tiberim … quattuor jūgerum colēbat agrum

    the one hope of the Roman people’s empire, Lucius Quinctius, was farming a field of four iugera across the TiberLiv. 3.26.8

  • amnem trānsitūrī minimōs praemittunt

    when they are about to cross a river, they send the smallest aheadPlin. NH 8.11

See also over, beyond, opposite, through.
